## Solution

Let $X \subset \mathbb{A}^n$ be cut out by $f_1, \dots, f_r \in k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, and let $p = (a_1,\dots,a_n)$ be a $k$-valued point at which $X$ is regular of dimension $d$.

**Regularity hypothesis, restated.** The local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X,p}$ is a regular local ring of dimension $d$, equivalently (since $X$ is cut out in the smooth ambient $\mathbb{A}^n$ of dimension $n$) the Jacobian matrix
$$
J(p) \;=\; \left(\frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_j}(p)\right)_{\substack{i=1,\dots,r \\ j=1,\dots,n}} \;\in\; k^{r \times n}
$$
has rank exactly $n - d$. (This is the Jacobian criterion for regularity on affine space: $\dim \mathcal{O}_{X,p} = n - \operatorname{rank} J(p)$, and regularity means the embedding dimension $n - \operatorname{rank} J(p)$ equals the Krull dimension $d$.)

**Definition.** The *tangent $d$-plane* to $X$ at $p$, denoted $T_p X$, is the affine linear subspace of $\mathbb{A}^n$ passing through $p$ defined by the linear system
$$
\boxed{\;\sum_{j=1}^{n} \frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_j}(p)\,(x_j - a_j) \;=\; 0, \qquad i = 1, \dots, r.\;}
$$

Equivalently, writing $\bar x = (x_1,\dots,x_n)$ and $\bar a = (a_1,\dots,a_n)$,
$$
T_p X \;=\; \bigl\{\, \bar x \in \mathbb{A}^n \;\big|\; J(p)\,(\bar x - \bar a)^{\mathsf T} = 0 \,\bigr\}.
$$

**Why it is a $d$-plane.** The defining equations are $r$ linear equations in the $n$ variables $(x_j - a_j)$, centered at the origin of the translated coordinate system. Their solution set is an affine linear subspace through $p$ whose dimension equals
$$
n - \operatorname{rank} J(p) \;=\; n - (n - d) \;=\; d.
$$
Hence it is genuinely a $d$-dimensional affine linear subspace — a "$d$-plane" — as claimed.

**Coordinate-free / intrinsic description.** The same subspace is the Zariski tangent space of the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X,p}$:
$$
T_p X \;\cong\; \operatorname{Hom}_k\!\bigl(\mathfrak m_p/\mathfrak m_p^2,\, k\bigr),
$$
where $\mathfrak m_p \subset \mathcal{O}_{X,p}$ is the maximal ideal of $p$. Regularity of $\mathcal{O}_{X,p}$ of dimension $d$ means $\dim_k(\mathfrak m_p/\mathfrak m_p^2) = d$, so this dual vector space is $d$-dimensional; translating back to $\mathbb{A}^n$ via the embedding $X \hookrightarrow \mathbb{A}^n$ recovers exactly the affine linear subspace defined above. The linear equations $\sum_j \frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_j}(p)(x_j - a_j) = 0$ are precisely the image of $df_i|_p$ under the identification of the cotangent space of $\mathbb{A}^n$ at $p$ with the span of $\{dx_j\}$, and the tangent $d$-plane is their common kernel translated to pass through $p$.

**Well-definedness (independence of the chosen equations).** If $X$ is also cut out by another set $g_1,\dots,g_s$, then the ideal $(f_1,\dots,f_r) = (g_1,\dots,g_s) = I(X)$ (at least locally at $p$, which suffices for the tangent space). Each $g_\ell$ is a linear combination $\sum_i h_{\ell i} f_i$ near $p$, so by the Leibniz rule
$$
dg_\ell|_p \;=\; \sum_i h_{\ell i}(p)\, df_i|_p \;+\; \sum_i f_i(p)\, dh_{\ell i}|_p \;=\; \sum_i h_{\ell i}(p)\, df_i|_p,
$$
since $f_i(p) = 0$ (the $f_i$ vanish on $X$, hence at $p$). Thus the row space of $J_g(p)$ is contained in that of $J_f(p)$, and by symmetry they are equal. The common kernel — and hence the tangent $d$-plane — is therefore independent of the choice of defining equations.

---

**Summary.** The tangent $d$-plane to $X$ at the regular point $p$ is the affine linear subspace of $\mathbb{A}^n$ through $p$ cut out by the linearized equations $\sum_{j=1}^n \frac{\partial f_i}{\partial x_j}(p)(x_j - a_j) = 0$ for $i = 1,\dots,r$. Its dimension is $n - \operatorname{rank} J(p) = d$ by the regularity hypothesis, and it is intrinsic to $X$ (independent of the chosen generators $f_i$), coinciding with the Zariski tangent space $\operatorname{Hom}_k(\mathfrak m_p/\mathfrak m_p^2, k)$ embedded in $\mathbb{A}^n$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
